The three-layer metamaterial is based on orthogonal double split-ring resonators (ODSRs) and metal ground planes separated by lossy dielectric substrates.
Copper with conductivity 5.8 × 10^7 S/m and thickness 0.036 mm is used for the metallic layers.
Modified epoxy substrates have relative permittivity 4.2 and loss tangent 0.02.
The metamaterial achieves absorptivity greater than 90% from 5.66 GHz to 15.10 GHz.
Multiple absorption peaks occur at 4.75, 6.06, 8.72, 12.52, and 14.86 GHz.
The metamaterial array is loaded on the antenna ground's weak current area with a radius of 17 mm.
Simulated impedance bandwidth of the antenna with metamaterial is 5.58–5.82 GHz with S11 < –10 dB.
Gain increases from 6.06 dBi (common antenna) to 8.27 dBi (with metamaterial) at 5.65 GHz.
3-dB beamwidth of E-plane reduces from 156° to 80°, and H-plane from 62° to 57° with metamaterial loading.
Measured ultra-wideband RCS reduction bandwidth is 4.72–18 GHz for x-polarized waves and 4.46–12 GHz for y-polarized waves.
Maximum measured RCS reduction is 18.4 dB at 8.7 GHz (x-polarized) and 22.5 dB at 6.3 GHz (y-polarized).
Cross-polarization components increase due to coupling between metamaterial and antenna slot.
The antenna prototypes were fabricated using common PCB methods on modified epoxy substrates of 1 mm and 1.5 mm thickness.
Experimental impedance bandwidth of the metamaterial antenna is 5.49–5.82 GHz (5.8%), slightly shifted due to fabrication tolerance.
The metamaterial antenna outperforms previous designs in terms of RCS reduction bandwidth and gain enhancement.
The absorption mechanism is explained by interference and dielectric loss in the three-layer metamaterial structure.
Simulations and measurements show good agreement in RCS reduction and radiation patterns.
The metamaterial array elements are arranged periodically on the antenna ground.
The study uses both radiating and scattering performance to evaluate the antenna.
